title: MRIS
subtitle: Mountain Rescue Information System
summary: Enterprise mountain rescue platform focused on production system development, integration, and long-term maintenance.

overview.title: Overview
paragraphs: MRIS is the primary production system I work on as a Software Development Engineer at eZoom Information.
I contribute to full-stack feature development, production maintenance, system integration, and deployment while working within a large existing enterprise application.

responsibilities.title: Responsibilities
items: Develop and maintain full-stack features across Vue frontends and .NET backend services within a large production system.
Participate in system analysis, feature planning, database design, and REST API implementation throughout the development lifecycle.
Design and optimize PostgreSQL data models and implement business workflows including CRUD operations, search, filtering, and pagination.
Deploy, maintain, and troubleshoot applications running on Windows Server and IIS, ensuring reliable production operation.
Investigate and resolve issues spanning frontend, backend APIs, databases, authentication, routing, and deployment environments.
Continuously improve system maintainability through incremental enhancements, technical documentation, and architectural refinements.

technical_highlights.title: Technical Highlights
paragraphs: MRIS is a mature enterprise system where implementing a feature often requires understanding interactions across multiple services rather than a single codebase. The project emphasizes end-to-end thinking, from user interfaces and backend services to databases, deployment, and operational infrastructure.

Working in this environment strengthened my ability to navigate complex systems, troubleshoot production issues across technical boundaries, and improve maintainability through incremental engineering practices.

items.title: System integration across multiple teams
items.description: The platform integrates services developed by different internal teams and external vendors. Delivering new features often requires understanding existing interfaces, coordinating changes across systems, and maintaining compatibility without disrupting established workflows.

items.title: Maintaining compatibility across versions
items.description: Enterprise systems evolve continuously, making backward compatibility and controlled releases essential. New functionality must integrate with existing modules while minimizing risk to production environments and ongoing operations.

items.title: Rapid production troubleshooting
items.description: Production issues can originate from frontend applications, backend services, databases, authentication, routing, deployment, or infrastructure. Effective troubleshooting requires tracing requests across the entire system to identify root causes and restore normal operation quickly.

outcome.title: Outcome
paragraphs: Working on MRIS has provided hands-on experience developing and maintaining large-scale production systems. Beyond feature implementation, the project has strengthened my understanding of enterprise software development, cross-team collaboration, and long-term system maintenance.
highlights: Contributed to a production enterprise system used in daily operations.
Delivered incremental improvements while preserving system stability.
Built practical experience across the complete software lifecycle.

lessons_learned.title: Lessons Learned
items: Building enterprise software requires understanding existing systems before introducing new solutions.
Long-term maintainability comes from clear architecture, stable interfaces, and incremental improvement rather than large-scale rewrites.
Successful production troubleshooting depends on understanding how every layer of a system works together, not just the code being changed.
